title: pvXMLMultiBlockDataReader
body:
## pvXMLMultiBlockDataReader

Reads VTK XML multiblock files (.vtm, .vtmb) into a multiblock dataset whose named blocks are read from the serial VTK XML files the .vtm meta file lists, with the selected point and cell arrays and any field data. The VTK XML formats keep every array as written, so this is the natural way to reload data saved by ParaView, VTK or Schemaxis exports. Several file names form a time series. Use readMultiBlock for the simple single-file case; PieceDistribution only matters in parallel.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The .vtm file is a meta file; the block files it lists (usually in a folder of the same name) must stay with it.
- Arrays left out of CellArrayStatus or PointArrayStatus are not read; name the arrays later nodes need.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this reader, so check the output on your own files.

Native constructor: `XMLMultiBlockDataReader`. Identity: `sources/XMLMultiBlockDataReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellArrayStatus` | Names of the cell-centred arrays to read, i.e. values stored on the block cells in the VTK XML multiblock file's CellData. Arrays not listed are skipped, saving memory and read time; an empty list reads the geometry without cell arrays. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileName` | VTK XML multiblock meta files (.vtm or .vtmb) to read. One file gives one multiblock dataset; several files are read as a file series, one time step per file in the order listed. Each .vtm refers to serial VTK XML block files, which must stay with it. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"items":{"minLength":1,"type":"string"},"minItems":1,"type":"array"}` | `required` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `PieceDistribution` | Control how datasets are loaded in parallel. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Block","Interleave"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Block"` |
| `PointArrayStatus` | Names of the point-centred arrays to read, i.e. values stored at the block points in the VTK XML multiblock file's PointData. Arrays not listed are skipped, saving memory and read time; an empty list reads the geometry without point arrays. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `TimeArray` | Names the field-data array that holds the time value of each time step (ParaView's XML default is TimeValue). Choose the entry "None" to number the steps with the integers 0, 1, 2, ... instead of reading a time array. ParaView's own description calls that entry "Default", but the list's no-selection entry is "None". | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvXMLMultiBlockDataReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": [
      "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
    ]
  }
}
```
